decision: Require coordinator-side filesystem enforcement verification before read-only Qubes Phase-1 qualification.
winner: service-identity permission gate on durable files plus parent directories

criteria.correctness: Proves the service identity cannot obtain file write permission or a writable descriptor and cannot atomically replace durable files through a writable parent directory.
criteria.robustnessSecurity: Fail-closed on symlinks, non-regular files, unexpected filesystem errors, writable files, writable descriptors, or writable parent directories. Performs no write and exposes no durable-state contents.
criteria.latency: Qualification-only local filesystem permission checks; no production qrexec round trip is added.
criteria.resourceUse: No daemon, watcher, database, WAL, polling loop, or persistent process state.
criteria.regressionRisk: Thin precondition gate composed ahead of the existing Phase-1 collector; MissionQueue, WorkerRuntime, transport framing, and attestation semantics are unchanged.
criteria.qa: Unit regressions cover verified read-only state, writable files, writable descriptors, writable parent directories, and symlink fail-closed behavior. Runner regression rejects qualification when enforcement is not verified.

alternatives.reason: Detects durable drift but does not prevent writes and can miss a short write-and-rollback entirely between snapshots.

alternatives.approach: persistent filesystem watcher or audit daemon
alternatives.reason: Adds lifecycle, platform, resource, and operational complexity while still being observational rather than a prevention boundary.
Mode bits alone do not prove effective permission for the actual service identity and ignore atomic replacement through writable parent directories.

knownLimitations: This gate must execute as the same coordinator-side identity/context that runs the Phase-1 qrexec service.
Filesystem permissions do not replace Qubes qrexec policy isolation or deployment identity/attestation checks.
A more privileged process outside the service identity may still mutate state; this gate establishes the service-specific boundary only.
lessons: Zero-mutation evidence and zero-mutation capability are different properties; REAL-WORKER gating needs both observation and prevention.
Read-only files are insufficient when the containing directory permits rename/unlink/atomic replacement.
Qualification should prefer prevention controls that add no production data-plane round trips.
safety: Synthetic/defensive qualification only; no real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflow, or security-control weakening.
